name: Dum Aloo Lucknowi
subtitle: fried baby potatoes finished in a yogurt gravy with fennel and dry ginger, no onion or garlic

ingredients.qty: 500g baby potatoes, boiled 10 minutes and peeled

ingredients.note: use compounded-free hing to keep the dish gluten-free
saunth stands in for fresh ginger in a no-onion-garlic kitchen

prepNotes: Boil the potatoes only until a skewer goes in with slight resistance, then cool and peel. Fully soft potatoes collapse in the fryer.
Prick each peeled potato all over with a fork or toothpick — that is how the gravy gets inside.
Whisk the yogurt with the dry spices before it goes in the pan; the powders stop it splitting.

steps.text: Prick the boiled, peeled potatoes deeply all over and pat them dry.
Deep fry them in hot oil until golden and lightly blistered, 4–5 minutes. Drain and set aside.
steps.tip: Dry potatoes only — wet ones spit violently in hot oil.

steps.text: Whisk the yogurt with the coriander powder, kashmiri chilli, turmeric, fennel powder and dry ginger powder to a smooth, lump-free mix.
Heat the ghee in a kadhai, add the bay leaf, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and cumin seeds and let them crackle 30 seconds.
Add the asafoetida, count to five, then immediately pour in the spiced yogurt.
steps.tip: Hing burns in seconds. It goes in last and the yogurt follows straight after.

steps.text: Cook on the lowest flame, stirring without stopping, for 7–8 minutes until the mixture thickens and the ghee separates.
steps.tip: Stop stirring and it curdles. This is the one step that needs your full attention.

steps.text: Add the fried potatoes and salt and turn them through the masala for 3 minutes.
Pour in 250ml warm water, bring to a simmer, then cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes.
Uncover, stir in the garam masala and crushed kasuri methi and reduce 3 minutes until the gravy clings to the potatoes.
Rest covered 5 minutes before serving with sheermal or plain rice.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and the potatoes absorb more flavour overnight. Reheat covered on low with a splash of water. Do not freeze — the potatoes turn grainy.
